§1 — Why the structure must come from documents

The prediction in filter-grounding-prediction only counts if the 2023 configuration is taken from documents. If it were read off the 2023 data, the prediction would be a fit to its own validation set. The evidence in jt60sa-booster-ripple-evidence leaves four facts open (§8 there). §2 owns the booster's bridge arrangement. §3 owns the as-built state of the grounding system and of each booster's filter, EF6's included. §4 owns the operation logs. §5 replaces the literature excerpts the other three rely on with page-referenced full texts. Every fact goes into one sources register: the source table in jt60sa-booster-ripple-evidence §2, extended with a page and a quotation for each row. Each section's evidence fragment keeps the search log behind its rows, not a second copy of the table. A fact found only in our own data analysis is not a source. Every source searched also records one fact known to be present in it, found by the same search, so a not-found entry is a demonstrated absence rather than an unread document.

§2 — The booster's bridges and transformers

Find, for each booster, three things:

  • the number of thyristor bridges and how they are connected (series or parallel, one or two transformers);
  • the transformer phase groups, which fix any phase shift between bridges;
  • the rated line voltage and leakage reactance, inherited from JT-60U.

Also establish whether the 2023 operation runs the bridges as a 30° pair. Places to look:

  • the report that page 8 of the MECS v2.9.2 overview reproduces as an image. Its captions read "Figure 2.7-20 Scheme of the filter for reducing the voltage ripple generated by Booster PS" and "Table 2.7-18 Main specification of Booster ripple reduction filter components", so it is a design document with a chapter 2.7 on the booster filter, most likely the filter's procurement specification; the deck itself carries no such numbering in its text;
  • the SNU/Booster slides' embedded EMF drawing (data/sources/SNU,Booster.pptx, needing an EMF converter);
  • the JT-60SA power-supply papers and their JT-60U predecessors;
  • the MECS input file ps_limit_table.dat documentation.

Done when the register cites a document for bridge count, connection and phase shift, and gives the line voltage and leakage reactance with their source. A schematic we draw from those citations is in docs/figures/jt60sa-power-supply-sources/booster-circuit.svg, written by scripts/figures/jt60sa_supply_circuits.py with power_convertor.style; §7's base-supply schematic comes from the same script. Any fact still uncited is listed as open, with the places searched and, for each, the known-present fact that search did find.

§3 — The grounding system and the filters as built

Establish when the grounding system entered service, its topology, and its resistor values, and check them against the MECS Simulink network (2 kΩ and 45 kΩ mid-point resistors). Establish for each of the four boosters when its filter was installed and commissioned. EF6 matters most: its 2023 ripple behaves as if the trap were absent. Read the papers on the 2023 coil energisation tests and the magnet system's commissioning performance.

Done when the register gives, with citations, the grounding system's in-service date, topology and resistor values, and each booster filter's installation state for the 2023 shots used here (E100863, E100865, E100882). Any of these still not found is listed with the documents read and the known-present fact each search found.

§4 — The operation logs for the two campaigns

The daily operation reports (3,759 pages, /JT60SA_TWIKI/data/Main/SystemDailyReport*.txt on nakasvr23) and the power-supply team's shift logs cover the 2021 tests and the 2023 restart. Retrieve the entries for February–March 2021 and August–December 2023. Index every one that mentions the boosters, the filter, grounding, twelve-pulse operation or EF6, with date, shot and quotation. nakasvr23 is retired, and the former Main web is not on its replacement, nakasvr26: every probe of the daily reports there returns 404 (AGENTS.md, 2026-10-13). The only known copies are the pages the imas-codex graph ingested from ssh://jt-60sa/var/www/html/twiki/. Index those, and record which months of the two campaigns they cover and which they do not. For the gaps, name who at QST holds the archive and what to ask for.

Positive control: before the campaign search, the fragment names one daily-report page the graph holds, with its date and one sentence quoted from it, so the index check has an entry known to be present. If the graph holds no daily-report page at all, the fragment shows the query that found none beside the same query's hit on another page type ingested from the same TWiki path, so an empty index is a measured absence and not a failed search. Negative control: the index check re-reads every entry, the positive control included, against the ingested pages, and a deliberately altered quotation or a mismatched report date is rejected.

Done when the index exists in this section's evidence fragment, covering both campaigns. It states the number of reports read, the number matched and the search terms, so a reader can see that an absent topic was searched for and not found.

§5 — The literature in full

The quotations in the evidence document came from search excerpts. Obtain the full texts and replace each excerpt with a page-referenced quotation:

  • JT-60SA Newsletter No. 118;
  • "Recent progress of JT-60SA project toward plasma operation" (Nuclear Fusion, 2024);
  • "Global cryogenic Paschen test of the JT-60SA magnet system" (Fusion Engineering and Design, 2023);
  • "Coil energization tests in JT-60SA integrated commissioning" (Fusion Engineering and Design, 2025);
  • "Performance of the JT-60SA superconducting magnet system during integrated commissioning" (Nuclear Fusion).

The automated fetches were refused (certificate error, HTTP 403), so this may need the lead's institutional access.

Done when every quotation in the evidence document §6 carries a page reference to a full text held in data/sources/. A quotation still marked excerpt-only names the routes tried, and at least two of the five texts are held in full, so the section cannot close on access failures alone.

§6 — Plant data outside EDDB

Every channel used so far comes from EDDB at 4 kHz. Four quantities would test the model more directly but are not in the EDDB catalogue: the motor-generator's frequency and voltage, the coil terminal-to-ground voltages that would show the grounding system working, the filter branch currents (the filter specification lists two current transducers per booster, rated ±1200 A), and any power-supply channel sampled faster than 4 kHz, which would remove the aliasing above 2 kHz. On nakasvr26, PMDB (plant data) has no channel catalogue, and keyed probes returned irc 301 on 2026-10-08. The FSMD and EASY libraries, the likely homes of fast-sampled data, are missing. Find the plant channel names from documents (HMI lists, plant data lists, the power-supply operation logs), probe PMDB with them, and establish who can grant FSMD or EASY access. The probe extends scripts/jt60sa/probe_shots.py, which already reads channels by name and records ok and irc per probe, and runs through scripts/jt60sa/run_remote.sh; a second prober is written only if PMDB's interface cannot be reached through it, with the reason recorded.

A faster channel helps only if it resolves the band the model is judged on, up to 30f (about 1.84 kHz), without aliasing. That needs a native rate comfortably above twice that, and an anti-alias response that is documented or measured. A channel with unknown acquisition filtering is recorded as such and is not counted as alias-free.

Done when each of the four quantities is either read for at least one 2021 and one 2023 booster shot and saved to data/jt60sa/, with its native sample rate and acquisition filtering stated, or recorded as unavailable with the routes tried. A PMDB channel known to exist, read successfully by the same route, proves the route works before any absence is recorded. Negative control: a deliberately misspelled channel name, or a read that returns an error code, is kept out of the acquired set, shown by the probe's own record.

§7 — The base supplies' converters, both families

The base supplies are a second ripple source on every coil, and the filter does not act on them (jt60sa-booster-ripple-evidence §9). With every supply running and almost no current, CS1–4, EF1 and EF6 put 310–390 V on the 6f line and about 80 V on 18f, while EF2–EF5 put about 130 V on 12f and behave as twelve-pulse converters. The documents described so far call all ten base supplies 12-pulse, four-quadrant converters, which explains EF2–EF5 but not the first family.

Find, for each family:

  • the converter arrangement: bridge count, series or back-to-back connection, transformer secondaries and their phase shift, and the circulating-current reactor if there is one;
  • the operating mode near zero current (circulating-current or blocking), which sets the even lines; the CS coils carry 100–115 V at 12f in some 2023 shots and about 2 V in others;
  • the rated line voltage and leakage reactance;
  • which party procured and built each family, since the split may follow the procurement;
  • what volPSDC measures, given that CS1, EF1 and EF6 carry one identical 71 V line at 6f on it.

Places to look: the EU power-supply overview paper and the JT-60SA power supply system paper (both in §5), the MECSfeat wiki page, and the MECS Simulink model of the base supplies.

Done when the register cites a document for each family's arrangement, phase shift and operating mode near zero current, and a schematic drawn from those citations is in docs/figures/jt60sa-power-supply-sources/base-supply.svg. Positive control: the cited arrangement predicts the measured family signature at zero current (6f and 18f present with the even lines nearly absent, or 12f present with 6f and 18f absent). Negative control: the same arrangement with its phase shift set to 0° predicts a signature the measured lines rule out for that family, so the check can tell a correct arrangement from a wrong one. Any fact still uncited is listed as open with the places searched and, for each, a known-present fact the same search did find.

§8 — The cited schematics

§2 and §7 closed on their registers. scripts/figures/jt60sa_supply_circuits.py draws from those registers into docs/figures/jt60sa-power-supply-sources/. Its base-supply.svg already shows the ENEA two-phase-group and CEA four-phase-group families, and booster-circuit.svg the booster bridges. What is owed is the citation binding: the script's sources are a free-text comment block tied to no register row, and tests/test_supply_circuits.py checks netlist topology only, so nothing fails when a drawn element loses its source.

Done when booster-circuit.svg shows each booster as four converters in two series and antiparallel pairs with transformers 30° apart, and base-supply.svg shows the ENEA two-phase-group and CEA four-phase-group families. The script holds its citations as data: each drawn element is keyed to a register row carrying document and page, and the figure's caption or a label beside the element states it. A test in tests/test_supply_circuits.py checks that every drawn element has a row. Negative control: removing one element's register row makes that test fail and name the element.

§9 — Other routes to the missing plant data: the wiki's manuals and the codex graph

§6 found none of the four quantities through the documented routes: coil terminal-to-ground voltage, filter branch current, motor-generator frequency and voltage, and a supply channel faster than 4 kHz. Before an outside request goes to QST, look for routes §6 did not try.

  • The Code wiki on nakasvr26 (topic index WebTopicList.html), for access manuals and channel lists: PMDB, FSMD and EASY, the HMI and plant-data lists, the motor-generator and power-supply recorders, and the quench-protection and grounding measurements.
  • The imas-codex graph, which has ingested JT-60SA wiki pages and the EDDB catalogue. Search it for the same topics and for circuit-node voltages not yet fetched: volSNUAT, volQPCDR, volQPCAT, volDR, and the FPPC and error-field supplies. Reach it through the read-only MCP server (.mcp.json), or the imas-codex graph shell and discover commands.

Done when the fragment lists, for each of the four quantities, every route found: manual, channel name, library or contact, each with its source page. Each found channel is probed through scripts/jt60sa/probe_shots.py for one 2021 and one 2023 booster shot, with the result saved and its native rate stated, or recorded as unavailable with the reason. The fragment states whether a request to QST is still needed and exactly what it must ask for. Negative control: a channel named in no source must be refused by the same probe.

§10 — Committed tests for the plant probe

§6 and §9 extended scripts/jt60sa/probe_shots.py with PMDB reads, a failed-control refusal, error classification and named EDDB channels (--eddb-channel). Their gates rested on saved receipts. Both independent reviews scored durability below the floor, 7 and 6: no committed test exercises those branches, so removing the refusal or the named-channel insertion would leave every gate green.

Done when tests/test_probe_shots.py drives the script against controlled wrapper responses, with no site access, and covers four cases: a failed control suppresses every candidate read; error codes are classified as the script records them; --eddb-channel inserts the named channel into the request; and a known-present channel is read while an unknown one is refused. Each test fails when its branch is removed, shown by a mutation. The full tests/ directory passes.

§11 — The unprocessed database's live catalogue

§6 and §9 searched EDDB, PMDB, the wiki and the codex graph and found none of the four quantities. The route neither tried is UDDB, the unprocessed database. The JT-60SA DB-system paper (graph page jt-60sa:IntroductionOfJT60SADBSystem) defines unprocessed data as the primary source records that the discharge data are processed from, "with fast sampling frequency and/or high resolution". §9 read the Data Handbook's link to UDDB but did not list its live table, and the graph holds only 189 UDDB entries, all soft-X-ray PIDs from shot 101173. The other database names on the wiki are analysis or simulation stores (LCDB, MBDB, MDDB, EDASDB, LOCALDB, MAPDB, IMASDB), equilibrium stores (EQDB, FAME) or Fortran namelist switches (NEQDB, RADMDB). FSMD and EASY are JT-60U libraries absent from nakasvr26 (§6).

Read UDDB on nakasvr26 with /analysis/src/uddb/uddb_pwrapper.py and /analysis/lib/libuddb.so, as the graph's jt-60sa:edas:uddb access record gives them: uddbreadTable() for the alias list, uddbreadHeader(shot, pid), and uddbreadConvert(shot, pid, t1, t2, datavol, ch). Save the whole alias table. Select every PID whose alias, function or header names a PF coil (EF1–EF6, CS1–CS4), a power supply, a booster or base, a filter, the ground, a motor-generator, or the MMSYS coil-voltage acquisition. Read each selected PID's header for E100303 (2021) and E100865 (2023), giving the shot number in UDDB's own form. For 2023, read headers only: no 2023 waveform is read, so the held-out prediction stays untouched.

Done when the full alias table is saved with its row count. The fragment registers each selected PID with its alias, channel count and native sampling rate for both shots. If none is selected, the fragment records the search terms and how many rows each was applied to. Any PID faster than 4 kHz that carries a coil voltage, a module or branch current, a terminal-to-ground voltage or a motor-generator quantity is read for one 2021 booster window and saved with its native rate. The fragment states whether that PID is the source EDDB's MMSYS/vol<coil> is processed from. Positive control: the graph-listed PID 2111UA001 reads for shot 101173. Negative control: the same reader refuses a misspelled PID.

§ Decisions

Ask the QST EDAS Development Team for FSMD/EASY access and the PF terminal-to-ground and filter-current channel mappings?

The four plant quantities that would test the model most directly (terminal-to-ground voltage for the Paschen question, filter branch current for the shunt attachment, motor-generator frequency, a supply channel faster than 4 kHz) are not reachable through any documented route. The probe identified the QST EDAS Development Team as the support contact. This is an external request on the lead's behalf.

The lead chose to proceed on EDDB data and record the gap, after the wiki and the codex graph were searched (§9) and no route to the four quantities was found. The terminal-to-ground figures stay conditional on the measured coil voltage, and the request §9 specifies is ready if the lead reopens it.
